title: Design System: Davirson Novoa — Research Tear Sheet

display.purpose: The candidate name at the top of the document. Once per surface.

verdict.purpose: What this asset is, stated once, large, in Source Serif 4 and institutional blue.

figure.purpose: Large tabular numbers in the figures band and anywhere a number is set large.

lede.purpose: The single balanced thesis line under the name; capped at 40ch.

title.purpose: Article and row headings inside a section.

bodySmall.purpose: Dense rows, capability details, availability block, footer. The 14px floor.

label.purpose: Tracked-caps metadata: classification line, field labels, band labels. Never a sentence.

motion.name: sheet-settle
motion.purpose: The one authored moment. Rows settle in from opacity 0 / translateY(10px) / blur(3px), staggered in reading order across the document header only (60ms, 120ms, 180ms, 240ms, 260ms, 300ms, then 340ms + 70ms per figure). Runs from an already-visible default; fully disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: hover-opacity
motion.purpose: Filled buttons fade to 90% on hover. No transform, no lift.

motion.name: hover-color
motion.purpose: Outlined controls and links move border and text to institutional blue on hover.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.purpose: Global focus-visible ring. Never removed or restyled per component.

narrative.overview:
This is a document, not an interface. The reader is a hiring analyst who reads assets for a living: verdict at the top, figures in a ruled band, evidence below, disclosures at the foot. Everything the system does follows from that arrangement. Structure is carried by hairline rules and banded rows — the sheet's own grammar — and never by boxes floating over a ground. Light is the home state because the audience reads in a bright office and prints; dark is a real second theme re-stepped against its own ground (#0e1216), not an inversion of the light one.

The palette is a two-voice instrument on a paper ground. Institutional blue owns whole bands and every technical claim; amber marks human and purpose content only, and nothing else. Type is two faces, committed: Archivo for all UI and prose, Source Serif 4 reserved for figures set large and for the one verdict line. Figures are tabular everywhere, wired at the body so every column of numbers aligns without per-element work.

The build refuses, explicitly and by name, the dark developer-portfolio arrangement it replaced: mono type, neon accents, terminal chrome, and a terminal-styled navigation bar. It also refuses ornament that would make it feel like a product page — no cards, no shadows, no gradients, no glow.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-white ground with near-black ink; dark theme re-stepped, never inverted
Hairline rules and full-bleed tinted bands as the only structural devices
Institutional blue for data and technical claims; amber for human/purpose content only
Two faces: Archivo everywhere, Source Serif 4 for large figures and the verdict
Tabular figures at the body level; every number aligns
Zero shadows, zero cards, 3px radius on controls and nothing else
Motion in the register of print — rules drawn, rows settled, figures counted — readable at rest, on paper, and under reduced-motion

rules.name: The Amber Reservation Rule
rules.body: Amber marks human and purpose content only: availability, hiring, the career-transition passage. Every data point, metric, and technical claim wears institutional blue or ink. This rule is binding, it predates the redesign, and getting it backwards was a live review finding — an amber number is a bug.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: A surface has exactly two accents. If a new state needs a color, it takes one of the four verdict/status hues (pos, neg, live, building) — it does not invent a third accent.

rules.name: The Re-Stepped Dark Rule
rules.body: The dark theme is authored against #0e1216 with its own ink ramp and its own accent steps (blue lightens to #74b0e4, amber to #d9a05b). Never derive dark by inverting or filtering the light values; each step is chosen for contrast on its own ground.

rules.name: The Band, Not the Box Rule
rules.body: A region is set apart by a full-bleed tint (coldsoft, warmsoft, band) capped with a 1–2px rule. It is never set apart by a bordered, rounded, floating container.

rules.name: The 14px Floor Rule
rules.body: No prose is set below 14px. This answered a real accessibility complaint. The 12–12.5px step exists only for tracked-caps metadata labels — never for a sentence a reader has to read.

rules.name: The Serif-Is-A-Figure Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 appears only on numbers set large and on the single verdict line. A serif paragraph, a serif heading, or a serif button does not exist in this system.

rules.name: The Tabular Everywhere Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums with "tnum" 1, "cv05" 1 is wired at the body. Numbers align in columns across the whole document by default; nothing opts out.

rules.name: The Label-Is-A-Field Rule
rules.body: Tracked caps label a field, a band, or the document itself (the classification line, which is native to the form). They do not sit above a headline as a decorative kicker.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: No shadow, no glow, no gradient, no elevation of any kind. If a region needs to separate, it takes a rule or a band. A drop shadow anywhere in this system is a defect.

rules.name: The Rule-Weight Rule
rules.body: 1px rulesoft divides metadata; 1px rule divides content rows; 2px in ink, cold, or warm opens a major band and declares its voice.

rules.name: The Print-Register Motion Rule
rules.body: Everything that moves does something a printed sheet does: a rule is drawn across the page (scaleX from the left), a row settles into place, an indicator segment fills, a figure is counted to its reading. Nothing bounces, parallaxes, or scales under the pointer; hover is worth one pixel of lift and a hairline of colour. Stagger follows reading order and is carried by a --d custom property so server components can set it without becoming client components.

rules.name: The Nothing-Hides-Behind-Motion Rule
rules.body: A reveal state may never be the only thing between a reader and the content. Hidden states are scoped to .js and set pre-paint, so a reader without JavaScript never meets an invisible page; a 3-second boot timer reveals everything if the bundle never runs; and @media print forces every reveal visible, because paper has no scroll and nothing would ever intersect. A sheet that prints blank is a defect, not an effect.

rules.name: The One-Scale Rule
rules.body: The self-assessment is declared once and read everywhere. The front page and the CV render the same rows at the same levels; a second, lower version of the same scale further down the site reads to a screener as a self-declared downgrade on the page whose job is to prevent one.

dos: Do carry structure with hairline rules (1px rule/rulesoft) and full-bleed bands, and open a major band with a 2px rule in ink, cold, or warm.
Do reserve amber for human and purpose content — availability, hiring, the career-transition passage — and give every data point and technical claim to institutional blue or ink.
Do set every large figure in Source Serif 4, tabular, with its label and a note underneath.
Do keep prose at 14px or larger; use the 12–12.5px tracked-caps step only for metadata labels.
Do author the dark theme against its own ground (#0e1216) with re-chosen steps, and keep light as the default reading state.
Do link every figure to the artifact that proves it.
Do state a claim once, large, and let the band below verify it.
Do keep motion to the single .settle stagger on a document header and disable it fully under reduced-motion.
Do keep motion in the print register — draw a rule, settle a row, count a figure — and make every animated element readable at rest, in print, and under reduced-motion.
donts: Don't add a shadow, glow, or gradient. The system is flat; a box-shadow here is a defect.
Don't wrap content in a card. Removing cards was a review decision on all three surfaces; use a top rule plus optional tint instead.
Don't put amber on a number, a metric, a stack tag, or any technical claim.
Don't introduce a third accent hue; extend with the existing verdict/status tokens.
Don't ship mono type, neon accents, terminal chrome, or a terminal-styled navigation bar — this world was chosen specifically against them.
Don't set a paragraph, heading, or button in the serif; the serif means "this is a figure."
Don't derive the dark theme by inverting or filtering light values.
Don't hide a control behind a bare dim glyph where a short label would work — the language switch is labelled for exactly this reason.
Don't round a band, row, or block; radius belongs to controls (3px) and to the two elements whose meaning is round.
Don't use an icon font, emoji, or a third-party icon package; icons are inline SVG at a 1.3px stroke on a 16px box.
Don't let a reveal state be the only thing standing between a reader and the content: if it can't be seen without JS, without motion, or on paper, it is a defect.
Don't publish a self-assessment on one surface and a lower one on another; the skill scale is declared once and both surfaces read the same rows.
